To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

companies are not really interested in the socio-environmental issues of the communities in which they operate, but only in the economic and financial benefits that can be obtained from the implementation of Socio-Environmental Practices.
the face of socio-environmentally responsible companies is not what it seems.
socioenvironmental responsibility, when it is practiced, is a way to improve business performance and increase profits, which are the main goal of the companies.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the face of the Socio-Environmental responsibility that is hidden and that, in our opinion, deserves more visibility in the debate on this subject, as it reveals the real face of the business and its practices, which is far from what is published by the business and academic world.
the face of the socio-environmental responsibilities that companies show and the one they hide.
the “faces” of socio-environments that show and those that hide, which are revealed and those that are hidden.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of the current capitalist system, socio-environmental practices, in their essence and in their consequences for society, have the potential to be a double-edged sword.
the Socio-Environmental Responsibilities that companies practice are not as socially responsible as they seem.
the socio-environmental responsibilities are not only those that are shown, but also those that are hidden.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the socioenvironmental responsibility of companies is not only a question of ethics, but a question of power, and that the “face” that is shown to the public and to the academic world is a mask that hides the true face of socioenvironmental responsibility.

the face that companies present to society is the “face” of Socio-Environmental Corporate Responsibility, which is a “face” that is presented to the general public, to the media, to the academic world and, in a way, to the State.

, in order to be truly ethical and socially responsible, companies should not only focus on their socio-environmental practices, but also take into account the social and environmental impacts of their products and services, and of their own existence, in the context of their business model, in order to achieve a more balanced and sustainable relationship with the society and the planet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although companies have been able to build their own image of Socio-Environmental responsibility, this is only a mask, which covers the real face that companies have.

the socio-environmental discourse of companies, in the current context of the COVID-19 pandemic, has the potential to hide the face of responsibility, and thus legitimize a discourse of “green capitalism” and the exploitation of workers and nature.
the socio-environmental discourse of companies is not only an attempt to improve their image and reputation, but also to increase their power and control over their employees and consumers.
